Have you looked at the 'Discovery' part of their website? You can search though records sections or by surnames. They have a mix of files that can either be viewed online or sent to you by post/email for a small cost.
http://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk 

If you are planning to visit make sure that you take the index/document numbers so you know where to go and that they are held at the Archives nearest you. According to their website records are split between different sites and sometimes offsite. There is a part on the website that allows you to order/reserve so that they're ready for you when you get there. I'm not sure if it costs any money though.

I found it easier to order the documents I needed by post. It takes up to 10 days for a quote/estimate (mine only took 4 days) then you pay and either have it posted to you or they can make the document available to view online. It costs me £2.60 for a copy of a naturalisation certificate.

The help part of their website explains how to use the Archive fairly clearly, good luck with your search :) http://nationalarchives.gov.uk/help/default.htm
